metadata.title: Shareholder register, general meetings and board of directors: the product
metadata.description: Sttok keeps the shareholder register with numbered share ranges, runs general meetings and the board through to certified minutes, and manages incentive plans, company groups and their documents.
metadata.keywords: shareholder register, share ledger, general meeting, board of directors, company groups, beneficial owner, incentive plans

hero.title: Shareholder register, general meetings and board of directors in one platform
hero.description: Sttok keeps your company's corporate records: the shareholder register with numbered share ranges, general meetings and the board through to certified minutes, incentive plans and company groups. Every transaction is documented and signed in the same place.

clientsLabel: More than 250 clients keep their records in Sttok

modules.title: What Sttok does at every stage of a company's corporate life
modules.lede: Every module works on the same register. What changes in the register is reflected in the meeting, in the certificate and in the group chart.

groups.title: Shareholders and register
groups.summary: The official record of who owns what, and since when.

items.title: Official shareholder register
items.description: Register of partners or of registered shares, with share classes, numbered ranges and export in a format ready for legalisation.

items.title: Transfers and encumbrances
items.description: Sales, inheritances, gifts, splits and renumbering. Pledges, usufruct, bare ownership, co-ownership and options are kept as separate positions.

items.title: Ownership and value certificates
items.description: The certificate the bank or the notary asks for, and the value of the shares according to the company's valuation.

items.title: Onboarding from deeds
items.description: Sttok reads the deeds with AI, chains the transactions together and flags gaps in the history.

items.title: Shareholder portal
items.description: Each shareholder logs in and sees their position, their certificates and the meetings they are called to.

items.title: Creditors and convertible notes
items.description: Each convertible note with its creditor's record, alongside the rest of the company's register.

groups.title: General meetings and board
groups.summary: The company's governing bodies, from the notice to the certified minutes.

items.title: General meeting
items.description: Notice, attendance, signed proxies, early voting and live voting. The minutes are drafted from the results.

items.title: Board of directors
items.description: Notice with agenda, committees, minutes and certification of resolutions.

items.title: Officers and powers of attorney
items.description: Directors, administrators, attorneys and auditors with their term, the scope of each power and its registration.

items.title: Company rules
items.description: Articles of association and shareholder agreements organised by topic, with the majority each resolution requires and the calendar of obligations.

groups.title: Company groups
groups.summary: Every company in the group and who controls each one.

items.title: All companies on one screen
items.description: What is pending in each company of the group, sorted by deadline, with permissions per company.

items.title: Group chart
items.description: Subsidiaries and the chain of control on any date. A group company can be a shareholder of another.

items.title: Beneficial owner
items.description: Who holds more than 25% of the capital or the votes at the end of the chain, calculated from the registers.

items.title: New companies
items.description: Each company comes in with its history. If it has just been incorporated, Sttok reads the deed of incorporation.

groups.title: Incentive plans
groups.summary: Employee and management plans, connected to the register.

items.title: Phantom shares and stock options
items.description: Each plan with its instruments, its pool and the shareholder resolution that approves it.

items.title: Vesting and grants
items.description: Vesting schedule for each beneficiary, with their signed invitation letter.

items.title: Beneficiary portal
items.description: Each employee sees their grant, what has vested and the documents they have signed.

items.title: Tender offers and liquidity
items.description: Purchase windows on vested rights, with withholding and a record in the plan.

groups.title: Transaction simulator
groups.summary: The effect of a transaction before it is signed.

items.title: Capital increases and reductions
items.description: The effect of each transaction on the actual register, including the pool and note conversion.

items.title: Sales and convertible notes
items.description: Who ends up with what percentage after each step, chaining several transactions.

items.title: Liquidation waterfall
items.description: What each shareholder receives in a sale, with the preferences of each class.

items.title: Draft documents
items.description: The simulated transaction comes with its drafts in Word for the notary or the law firm.

groups.title: Secondary market
groups.summary: Sales between shareholders, recorded in the register.

items.title: Sell offers
items.description: A shareholder publishes how many shares they are selling, at what price and by when.

items.title: Buy offers
items.description: The company or a shareholder makes a purchase offer to several shareholders at once.

items.title: Order book
items.description: Average price, volume and status of each offer, with its history.

items.title: Recorded in the register
items.description: Each completed transaction is entered in the shareholder register with its documents. Available as an add-on module.

groups.title: Documents, signature and communications
groups.summary: What is signed and sent, filed by company.

items.title: Documents and minute books
items.description: A repository per company with minute books by governing body and financial year, ready for legalisation.

items.title: Electronic signature
items.description: Signature envelopes with reminders and deadlines. Included in the Advanced and Pro plans.

items.title: Certified communications
items.description: Every notice and every message is logged with its proof of delivery.

items.title: Sttok AI
items.description: Questions about the register in plain language, with the source linked in every answer.

situations.title: Frequent situations and what Sttok does in each one

rows.situation: The bank asks for a certificate of ownership
rows.action: It is generated from the register with today's data.

rows.situation: The general meeting has to be called
rows.action: Sttok prepares the notice, tracks proxies and drafts the minutes with the voting results.
It manages the pre-emption right with its notices and deadlines, and records the transfer by share range.

rows.situation: The register has to be legalised
rows.action: It exports the register in the format filed with the Companies Registry.

rows.situation: The register is years out of date
rows.action: It rebuilds the history from the deeds in a few minutes.

rows.situation: The group's beneficial owner has to be identified
rows.action: It calculates ultimate ownership across the whole chain of companies.
It records the inheritance, splits the share numbers among the heirs and sets up co-ownership with its representative.

onboarding.title: How your data gets into Sttok
paragraphs: Setting up a company takes a few hours. For groups with many companies, the time depends on the number of companies.
If the register is years out of date, Sttok rebuilds it from the deeds in a few minutes. If your data is in Excel, in Carta or with your law firm, migration is part of the same process.

figures.title: Companies that already keep their records in Sttok
figures.note: More than 250 clients manage more than 500 companies. The average of two companies per client reflects the group profile of Sttok's users.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the product

items.a: A Spanish platform for keeping the shareholder register, general meetings, the board of directors, incentive plans and company groups. More than 250 clients use it to manage more than 500 companies.

items.q: Does Sttok replace the shareholder register?
items.a: Sttok keeps the register of partners or of registered shares as the official record. It exports it in a format ready for legalisation and lets the company file it electronically with the Companies Registry when it decides to.

items.q: Can I manage every company in my group?
items.a: Yes. Each company has its own register, governing bodies and permissions, and one group company can be a shareholder of another. The chart shows the chain of control on any date.

items.q: How long does it take to get started?
items.a: A few hours per company. For groups with many companies, the time depends on the number of companies.
The secondary market is a separate add-on module. Integrated electronic signature is included in the Advanced and Pro plans.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.
Encrypted and hosted in the European Union. Sttok is ISO 27001 certified and complies with the GDPR.
